summary: The VerifyLeader receipt confirms the mechanism as a second, execution-grounded finding. On a real four-voter cluster with one voter demoted to nonvoter through the exported DemoteVoter contract (three voters, quorum two), comparison 1 holds complete: a leader partitioned together with the nonvoter was confirmed with a vote tally of 2 against a quorum of 2, still in state Leader, even though it could reach no other voter. The control holds complete too — the same leader with no peer on its side ended with tally 1 against quorum 2 and the verification failed — and the two results differ by exactly the one acknowledgement the nonvoter supplies, which is what the source says: quorumSize counts voters only, while the tally is incremented by notifyAll for every followerReplication, including the one startStopReplication creates for a nonvoter. The third comparison, on the consequence that the detached voters elected their own leader and committed index 6 while the interrupted leader stayed at applied index 4, came out unknown rather than holds or violated, and I traced that to my own admission scoping: the shared prerequisite alias admitted the control trial's baseline, and the control deliberately emits no peer-side event, so the machinery reported a missing admission. I recorded that as a harness defect, described the retained peer-side operands as an observation attached to the receipt rather than as a held comparison, and submitted a successor that differs only in the admission structure — a second prerequisite alias scoped to the interrupted case — for a fresh execution, since a changed comparison calls for one. I also promoted the behavior and the fact as knowledge entries so later work can rely on them at an exact revision, and left the counterevidence visible: the interrupted leader is still inside its own lease when it is confirmed, the control fails through lease step-down rather than a negative vote, and a deployment without nonvoters cannot reach the path.
